result.title: Correct Answers from Insufficient Histories: A Controlled Study of Agent Memory Evaluation
result.summary: An answer can match the reference for a complete agent history even when the reader's visible history does not determine it. We study this distinction using executable device logs. Our protocol separates reference agreement, certified evidence sufficiency, and context-appropriate behavior. Insufficiency requires two legal histories yielding byte-identical visible contexts but different answers; public chronology and query cutoffs certify sufficient prefixes. On 80 confirmation histories, Qwen3-32B matches 87 hidden references among 203 insufficient raw-prefix instances, with only seven appropriate abstentions. A fixed-input DeepSeek-V4-Flash replication matches 85 and abstains on 21 of the same 203 instances. Each reader makes 1,600 requests. Compact CSV's estimated appropriateness effects remain inconclusive: +3.16 percentage points, clustered 95% interval [0.00,6.57], for Qwen and +2.46, [-1.84,6.94], for DeepSeek. A separate held-out judge study achieves 99.38% correctness but retains support errors and truncations; a deterministic baseline solves all constructed cases. These results support an evaluation diagnosis across two hosted reader configurations, not gains for a general memory system or natural-language evidence assessment.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用可执行设备日志设计受控评测，区分参考答案一致、证据充分性认证与上下文适切行为，并在80条确认历史上测试两个 reader 的匹配与弃答表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「两条合法历史产生相同可见上下文但答案不同」的充分性判据，可能为核查 LVR 的 latent 状态是否保留任务必要证据，以及 STOP/弃答决策的评价提供方法线索。
